Which collector is the natural candidate to evaluate?

generalfeedback.text: ZGC trades a little throughput and memory for very short pauses, which suits latency-critical APIs. Parallel maximises throughput with longer pauses, the opposite of what's needed.

answer.text: Generational ZGC, which keeps pauses sub-millisecond regardless of heap size

questiontext.text:
A production service is unresponsive and you suspect a deadlock or threads stuck on a slow database. You have shell access to the host.

Which command gives you the evidence?

generalfeedback.text: A thread dump shows every thread's state and stack trace, including BLOCKED threads, the locks they wait on and any detected deadlock.

questiontext.text:
A new deployment is benchmarked with a load test that starts immediately after startup and runs for 30 seconds. The results are much slower than production.

What is the most likely flaw in the test?

generalfeedback.text: HotSpot compiles hot code after profiling it, so early requests run slower. Warm up the service before measuring.

answer.text: No warm-up: during the first period the JVM is still interpreting and JIT-compiling hot methods

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/2.5 Modules, packaging and runtime images (JPMS, jars, jlink)

questiontext.text:
Module ng.itlearning.fx has a public class ng.itlearning.fx.internal.Cache. Another module requires ng.itlearning.fx but fails to compile when it uses Cache.

Why?

generalfeedback.text: Strong encapsulation: public is not enough across modules. The package must be exported, possibly only to specific modules.

answer.text: The class needs a public constructor
Only exported packages are accessible to other modules; ng.itlearning.fx.internal isn't exported

questiontext.text:
Jackson throws InaccessibleObjectException when deserialising into DTOs in package ng.itlearning.fx.dto, which is exported.

What does the module need?

generalfeedback.text: exports allows access to public members only; reflective access to private fields needs opens.

answer.text: opens ng.itlearning.fx.dto (ideally only to the Jackson module, tools.jackson.databind in Jackson 3) to allow deep reflection

questiontext.text:
A consumer module should discover any number of RateProvider implementations at runtime without referencing their classes.

Which pair of directives and API achieves this?

generalfeedback.text: The service loader mechanism decouples consumers from providers; adding a provider module adds an implementation without recompiling the consumer.

answer.text: uses RateProvider in the consumer, provides RateProvider with Impl in each provider, and ServiceLoader.load(RateProvider.class)

questiontext.text:
During migration, a plain (non-modular) library jar is placed on the module path next to your named application module.

How is the library treated?

generalfeedback.text: Automatic modules bridge the classpath world and named modules during top-down migration. Jars on the classpath form the unnamed module instead.

answer.text: As an automatic module: named from Automatic-Module-Name or the file name, reading all modules and exporting all its packages

questiontext.text:
The security team wants smaller container images with fewer JDK components for a Spring Boot service.

Which tools produce a trimmed runtime?

generalfeedback.text: jdeps --print-module-deps lists what the application uses; jlink assembles a custom runtime with just those modules.

answer.text: jdeps to find the required modules, then jlink to build a runtime image containing only those modules

questiontext.text:
A module's public API returns types from module ng.itlearning.money. Every consumer has to add requires ng.itlearning.money themselves.

How can the API module spare its consumers that step?

generalfeedback.text: requires transitive grants implied readability: anyone who requires the API module can also read the money module.

questiontext.text:
On a Java 25 JDK, a file Hello.java contains only void main() { IO.println("hi"); }.

What happens with java Hello.java?

generalfeedback.text: JEP 512 finalised compact source files, instance main methods and java.lang.IO in Java 25.

answer.text: It runs and prints hi: compact source files and instance main methods are standard in Java 25

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/2.6 Debugging and troubleshooting

questiontext.text:
A transfer fails with DataIntegrityViolationException; further down the trace is Caused by: PSQLException: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "journal_reference_key".

What is the most useful reading of this trace?

generalfeedback.text: The last Caused by is usually the root cause; your own first frame shows where your code was involved.

answer.text: The top line is always the root cause, so the problem is in Spring
Spring has a bug in its exception translation
The root cause is a repeated journal reference hitting a unique constraint; find the first frame in your own package to see which call inserted it

questiontext.text:
A loop processes 20,000 transfers and fails only for reference TRF-2026-0193.

How do you stop the debugger exactly there?

generalfeedback.text: Conditional breakpoints suspend only when the expression is true.

answer.text: Restart the IDE in safe mode

questiontext.text:
A service catches an exception somewhere deep in a library and returns null, so the error never reaches your logs.

Which debugger feature finds where it is thrown?

generalfeedback.text: Exception breakpoints stop where the exception is thrown, even if it is later caught.

answer.text: A watch on a local variable
An exception breakpoint on that exception type

questiontext.text:
Requests time out every afternoon. CPU is low. Three thread dumps taken ten seconds apart show most http-nio threads parked in HikariPool.getConnection.

What does this indicate?

generalfeedback.text: Threads waiting in getConnection mean connections aren't being returned fast enough.

answer.text: The JVM has run out of heap
The database connection pool is exhausted; find what holds connections for long (slow queries, long transactions, leaks) rather than only enlarging the pool
A deadlock between two HTTP threads

questiontext.text:
Heap use grows after every full GC until the service fails with OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space.

What is the best next step?

generalfeedback.text: Growing post-GC heap suggests a leak; the dominator tree shows which references keep objects alive.

answer.text: Capture a heap dump (or enable HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError) and inspect the dominator tree for what retains the memory
Switch to a different garbage collector
Double the heap and close the ticket

questiontext.text:
Which logging practices make production problems easier to solve? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Correlation ids link a request's lines; parameterised logs with the exception keep the stack trace. Sensitive data must never be logged.

answer.text: Putting a correlation id in the MDC for each request and returning it to the client
Logging full request bodies including card numbers
Logging with parameters and passing the exception as the last argument
Catching exceptions and logging only e.getMessage()

questiontext.text:
A teammate wants to enable JDWP remote debugging on the production server to investigate a bug quickly.

What is the right response?

generalfeedback.text: Remote debugging is for local or isolated environments; production needs safe diagnostics.

answer.text: Allow it and disable the firewall temporarily
Allow it during business hours only
Allow it if the port is changed from 5005
Refuse: an open debug port allows arbitrary code execution; reproduce locally, or use logs, metrics and dumps

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.1 Relational design

questiontext.text:
A legacy account table stores branch_code, branch_name and branch_city on every account row. A branch was renamed and now some accounts show the old name and some the new one.

Which normal form is violated, and what is the fix?

generalfeedback.text: That is a transitive dependency (account → branch_code → branch_name). Storing branch facts once in a branch table removes the possibility of inconsistent copies.

answer.text: 3NF; branch_name and branch_city depend on branch_code, not on the account, so move them to a branch table referenced by account.branch_code
None; add a trigger to keep copies in sync
2NF; add branch_code to the primary key

questiontext.text:
A mobile app retries a transfer request after a network timeout. The database now has two identical debit rows for the same transfer reference.

Which schema change would have prevented the duplicate at the database level?

generalfeedback.text: A unique constraint makes the second insert fail no matter which service or retry attempted it. The application can then treat the failure as 'already processed' (idempotency).

questiontext.text:
You need every customer and their total October debits, including customers with zero debits. This query drops the zero-debit customers: ... FROM customer c LEFT JOIN account a ON ... LEFT JOIN txn t ON t.account_id = a.id WHERE t.direction = 'D' ...

How should it be fixed?

generalfeedback.text: A WHERE condition on the right-hand table removes rows where it is NULL, turning the outer join into an inner join. Conditions in ON keep unmatched customers.

answer.text: Move the conditions on txn (direction, date range) into the ON clause of the LEFT JOIN and use coalesce(sum(t.amount), 0)

questiontext.text:
Finance asks for accounts whose total debits in October exceeded ₦5,000,000.

Which clause filters on the aggregated total?

generalfeedback.text: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping and cannot use aggregates. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

answer.text: HAVING sum(amount) > 5000000 after GROUP BY account_id

questiontext.text:
Ops needs a list of every reference that appears in the ledger but not in the switch file, in the switch file but not the ledger, or in both with different amounts.

Which join type produces all three categories in one query?

generalfeedback.text: A full outer join keeps unmatched rows from both sides (NULLs on the other side) and matched rows, so missing and mismatched transactions all appear.

questiontext.text:
A customer statement must show each transaction with the balance after it, in posting order.

Which SQL feature computes this without collapsing rows?

generalfeedback.text: Window functions compute across related rows while keeping each row. A running sum ordered by posting time (with id as tie-breaker) gives the running balance.

answer.text: A window function: sum(signed_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY posted_at, id)

questiontext.text:
A designer proposes storing account balances and transaction amounts as DOUBLE PRECISION 'for speed'.

What should you recommend?

generalfeedback.text: Floating-point errors accumulate in sums and break reconciliation. NUMERIC is exact. PostgreSQL's MONEY type depends on locale settings and is generally discouraged.

answer.text: Accept; doubles are faster and accurate enough
The MONEY type, because it is locale-aware
NUMERIC(19,2) (or BIGINT minor units), because binary floating point cannot represent many decimal amounts exactly

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.2 Transactions, isolation levels and locking

questiontext.text:
A transfer service debits account A, then crashes before crediting account B. Afterwards A shows the debit and B shows nothing.

What was missing?

generalfeedback.text: Atomicity: statements in one transaction commit together or not at all. Without it, a crash between statements leaves partial work.

answer.text: Both updates (and the ledger inserts) inside one database transaction, so a failure rolls the debit back

questiontext.text:
Running at PostgreSQL's default isolation (Read Committed), two app instances each do: SELECT balance; check in Java; UPDATE account SET balance = <computed value>. Occasionally a withdrawal disappears.

Which change prevents this lost update most simply?

generalfeedback.text: The conditional update performs the check and the change atomically on the locked row. A result of 0 rows means insufficient funds. Read Committed alone does not stop read-then-write lost updates.

answer.text: Cache the balance in the application
Use one atomic statement: UPDATE account SET balance = balance - :amt WHERE id = :id AND balance >= :amt, and check the affected row count

questiontext.text:
Several worker instances poll a payment_job table for PENDING jobs. Sometimes two workers process the same job, sending a payment twice.

Which query pattern lets workers claim jobs safely without blocking each other?

generalfeedback.text: FOR UPDATE locks the claimed rows; SKIP LOCKED makes other workers skip them instead of waiting, so each job goes to exactly one worker. Locking the whole table would serialise all workers.

answer.text: SELECT ... WHERE status = 'PENDING' LIMIT 10 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, inside a transaction that marks them IN_PROGRESS
LOCK TABLE payment_job in every worker

questiontext.text:
A transfer locks the source account row first and then the destination. Under load, PostgreSQL logs 'deadlock detected' and aborts some transfers.

What is the best prevention?

generalfeedback.text: Transfers A→B and B→A lock in opposite orders. A consistent global order removes the cycle. Aborted transactions should still be retried, but prevention comes first.

answer.text: Lock both rows in a consistent order (e.g. by account id), for example SELECT ... WHERE id IN (:a, :b) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE

questiontext.text:
Customer profile edits are rare and users may keep the edit screen open for minutes. You want to stop one agent's save from silently overwriting another's.

Which technique fits best?

generalfeedback.text: Holding a row lock during minutes of user think-time blocks everyone else. Optimistic locking holds no locks and detects the rare conflict at save time.

answer.text: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE when the screen opens, held until save
Optimistic locking: a version column checked in the UPDATE's WHERE clause, with a 'someone else changed this' error on 0 rows

questiontext.text:
A service runs its transaction at SERIALIZABLE. In production, some requests fail with SQLSTATE 40001 'could not serialize access'.

What is the correct handling?

generalfeedback.text: Serialization failures are the expected mechanism by which Serializable guarantees correctness. The whole transaction must be retried, and idempotency (e.g. a unique reference) prevents duplicates.

answer.text: Retry the entire transaction from the beginning a few times with a short random backoff, provided the operation is idempotent
Ignore it; the data was saved
Treat it as a bug and lower the isolation level

questiontext.text:
A long-running monthly report query runs for 20 minutes on PostgreSQL. The payments team worries it will block card postings on the same tables.

What actually happens?

generalfeedback.text: MVCC gives the report a consistent snapshot without blocking writers. The cost of a long transaction is bloat from row versions VACUUM can't yet remove; reports often run on a replica for that reason.

answer.text: Under MVCC, readers don't block writers; postings continue, though very long transactions can delay VACUUM cleanup
The report sees postings as they happen
Postings are blocked until the report finishes

questiontext.text:
Two joint-account holders withdraw at the same time. Each transaction checks that the combined balance of both accounts stays ≥ 0, then debits a different account row. Both succeed and the combined balance goes negative, at Repeatable Read.

What is this anomaly, and what prevents it?

generalfeedback.text: Each transaction wrote a different row based on a read of both, so no write-write conflict occurred. Serializable isolation detects this pattern; explicit locking of both rows also prevents it.

answer.text: A dirty read; use Read Committed
A phantom read; add an index
Write skew; use SERIALIZABLE (with retries) or lock both rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before checking

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.3 Indexing and reading query plans in PostgreSQL and MySQL

questiontext.text:
The 'last 20 transactions' query WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY posted_at DESC LIMIT 20 takes 2 seconds. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows Seq Scan on txn with 'Rows Removed by Filter: 49,985,880', then a Sort.

Which index fixes both the scan and the sort?

generalfeedback.text: Equality column first, sort column second. The index finds account 42's entries already in posted_at order, so the planner reads 20 entries and stops. A hash index can't provide ordering.

answer.text: CREATE INDEX ON txn USING hash (account_id)
CREATE INDEX ON txn (account_id, posted_at DESC)

questiontext.text:
There is an index on txn(posted_at), but WHERE date(posted_at) = '2026-10-21' still does a sequential scan.

Why, and what is the fix?

generalfeedback.text: The index stores posted_at values, not date(posted_at). A half-open range on the raw column uses the index and avoids end-of-day boundary bugs.

answer.text: Wrapping the column in a function makes the predicate non-sargable; use a range: posted_at >= '2026-10-21' AND posted_at < '2026-10-22'
The index is corrupt; REINDEX it
date() is not supported in PostgreSQL

questiontext.text:
A composite index exists on (value_date, account_id). The query is WHERE account_id = ? AND value_date BETWEEN ? AND ? and it is still slow for busy date ranges.

What is the better index?

generalfeedback.text: With the range column first, the index must scan every account's entries across the date range. Putting the equality column first narrows straight to one account, then reads its date range.

answer.text: (account_id, value_date): equality column first, range column last

questiontext.text:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows the planner estimated 12 rows for a filter but 1,480,000 rows actually matched, and it chose a nested loop that ran for minutes. The table was bulk-loaded an hour ago.

What should you do first?

generalfeedback.text: A huge estimate-vs-actual gap points to stale statistics. After a bulk load, autovacuum may not yet have analysed the table. Fresh statistics usually fix the plan choice.

answer.text: Run ANALYZE on the table to refresh planner statistics, then re-check the plan

questiontext.text:
A payment table has 200 million rows, of which ~5,000 are PENDING at any time. Workers query WHERE status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 50.

Which index is most efficient?

generalfeedback.text: The partial index contains only the ~5,000 pending rows, already sorted by created_at: tiny, fast, and cheap to maintain.

answer.text: A partial index: CREATE INDEX ON payment (created_at) WHERE status = 'PENDING'

questiontext.text:
A DBA asks you to add an index to the 2-billion-row txn table in production during business hours.

How should it be created?

generalfeedback.text: A plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes for the whole build. CONCURRENTLY allows writes to continue, at the cost of a longer build, and can't run inside a transaction.

answer.text: LOCK TABLE txn first, then CREATE INDEX
CREATE INDEX inside the application's migration transaction
It cannot be done; take the bank offline
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, outside a transaction block, and monitor for failure (an invalid index must be dropped and retried)

questiontext.text:
In MySQL, EXPLAIN for a statement query shows type: ALL and Extra: Using where; Using filesort.

What does that tell you?

generalfeedback.text: type ALL is a full table scan; 'Using filesort' means rows are sorted after fetching. An index matching the filter and order removes both.

answer.text: A full table scan followed by an extra sort step: there's no suitable index for the filter and ORDER BY
The query is using the primary key
The query uses a covering index

questiontext.text:
The transaction ingestion job has slowed down as the team keeps adding indexes to txn.

Which statements about index cost are true?

generalfeedback.text: Indexes speed up reads but slow writes, use storage and compete for cache. Check usage statistics and drop indexes that never serve queries.

answer.text: Every INSERT must update every index on the table
Unused indexes still cost write time and storage
pg_stat_user_indexes.idx_scan helps find indexes that are never used

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.4 Schema migrations with Flyway and Liquibase

questiontext.text:
A developer fixes a typo in V3__add_account_daily_limit.sql, which already ran in UAT and production. The next deployment fails with a Flyway checksum mismatch.

What is the correct approach?

generalfeedback.text: Applied migrations are immutable history. Corrections go in new migrations so every environment converges the same way. Clean would drop production data.

answer.text: Revert the edit to V3 and put the correction in a new migration V6

questiontext.text:
Your team needs to rename account.number to account.nuban while the service runs as several instances with rolling deploys.

Which approach avoids breaking old instances during the deploy?

generalfeedback.text: During a rolling deploy, old code still reads number. Spreading the change over several backward-compatible releases keeps every running version working.

answer.text: Expand and contract: add nuban, write both, backfill, switch reads, then later drop number
Take the database offline over the weekend
ALTER TABLE account RENAME COLUMN number TO nuban in one release

questiontext.text:
A Flyway migration CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_txn_ref ON txn(reference); fails with 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block'.

How do you fix it?

generalfeedback.text: Flyway wraps each migration in a transaction by default, which CONCURRENTLY forbids. Removing CONCURRENTLY would block writes on a hot table during the build.

answer.text: Put it in its own migration and configure that script not to run in a transaction (executeInTransaction=false)

questiontext.text:
You need a reporting view that the analytics team changes often. You want it recreated whenever its definition changes.

Which Flyway migration type fits?

generalfeedback.text: Repeatable migrations re-run when their checksum changes, after all versioned migrations, which is ideal for views, functions and stored procedures.

answer.text: A repeatable migration R__view_name.sql with CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
A new versioned migration V__ for every change

questiontext.text:
The team is adopting Flyway on a 10-year-old production database that already has 140 tables and no migration history.

Which Flyway feature lets it start tracking from the current state?

generalfeedback.text: Baseline records the existing schema as a known version so Flyway only applies migrations newer than it.

answer.text: baseline (e.g. baseline version 1, with new changes as V2 onwards)

questiontext.text:
A migration adding a column needs an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on account, but a long-running report holds a conflicting lock. All payment queries queue up behind the waiting migration and the app freezes.

What precaution limits the damage?

generalfeedback.text: Lock requests queue in order; a waiting DDL lock blocks later queries too. A short lock_timeout makes the migration give up quickly, keeping production responsive.

answer.text: SET lock_timeout (e.g. '5s') at the start of the migration so it fails fast instead of queueing traffic behind it, then retry later

questiontext.text:
A bank's platform team standardised on Liquibase. You need to explain to a Flyway user how Liquibase identifies a change it has already applied.

Which answer is correct?

generalfeedback.text: Liquibase tracks changesets by id/author/file and stores checksums in DATABASECHANGELOG, whereas Flyway uses the version in the file name and flyway_schema_history.

answer.text: By the timestamp of the deploy
By the changeset's id plus author plus changelog file path, recorded in DATABASECHANGELOG

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.5 JDBC fundamentals

questiontext.text:
A statement-search endpoint builds SQL as "... WHERE narration LIKE '%" + q + "%'". A pentester sends q = %' UNION SELECT bvn, full_name, null FROM customer --.

What is the correct fix?

generalfeedback.text: Placeholders send the value separately from the SQL, so it can never change the statement's structure. Hand-escaping and keyword blocklists are fragile; least privilege helps but doesn't fix the bug.

answer.text: Use a PreparedStatement: WHERE narration LIKE ? with ps.setString(1, "%" + q + "%")
Run the query as a read-only user only

questiontext.text:
An API lets clients sort transactions by a sort query parameter (date or amount). A developer tries ORDER BY ? with ps.setString and the sort has no effect.

How should dynamic sort columns be handled?

generalfeedback.text: Placeholders bind values, not identifiers, so ORDER BY ? sorts by a constant. An allow-list keeps identifiers safe; concatenating raw input reintroduces injection.

answer.text: Map allowed values to column names with an allow-list (e.g. date → posted_at) and reject anything else
Sort in Java after loading all rows
Concatenate the parameter directly into the SQL

questiontext.text:
After a day in production, every request fails with Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms. Database CPU is idle. Code review finds Connection c = ds.getConnection(); with c.close() only on the success path.

What's the cause and fix?

generalfeedback.text: Each exception leaked one pooled connection until none were left. try-with-resources always returns them. A bigger pool only delays the outage.

answer.text: Use DriverManager instead of a pool
Connections leak on exception paths and the pool runs dry; use try-with-resources (and leakDetectionThreshold to find others)
The pool is too small; set it to 500

questiontext.text:
A nightly job inserts 2 million settlement rows one INSERT at a time with auto-commit on. It takes 3 hours.

Which change gives the biggest improvement?

generalfeedback.text: Row-by-row auto-commit means 2 million round trips and 2 million commits. Batching and fewer commits cut both dramatically; COPY is fastest for bulk loads. More indexes would slow it further.

answer.text: Turn off auto-commit, use addBatch/executeBatch in chunks (e.g. 1,000) and enable reWriteBatchedInserts=true, or use COPY
Add more indexes to the table
Run the job twice in parallel without changes

questiontext.text:
An import retried after a partial failure throws SQLException with SQLState 23505 on a reference that was already inserted.

What does 23505 mean, and a good way to make the import safely re-runnable?

generalfeedback.text: 23505 is unique_violation. With a unique reference plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, re-running the file is harmless: existing rows are skipped.

answer.text: Unique violation; make the insert idempotent with ON CONFLICT (reference) DO NOTHING (or treat 23505 as 'already processed')

questiontext.text:
A query reads a nullable overdraft_limit BIGINT column with rs.getLong("overdraft_limit"). Customers with no overdraft (NULL) are treated as having a limit of 0, and some logic depends on telling them apart.

How do you read the NULL correctly?

generalfeedback.text: Primitive getters return 0 for NULL. getObject with a wrapper class returns null, preserving the difference between 'no limit' and 'limit of zero'.

answer.text: Change the column to NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 silently
Use rs.getObject("overdraft_limit", Long.class), which returns null for SQL NULL (or check rs.wasNull())

questiontext.text:
A transfer runs two UPDATE statements through JDBC with the default connection settings. The second update fails, but the first one (the debit) remains in the database.

What was missing?

generalfeedback.text: In auto-commit mode each statement commits immediately. Grouping them in a manual transaction makes the transfer atomic.

answer.text: conn.setAutoCommit(false) before the statements, then commit() on success and rollback() on failure
A finally block that prints the error

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/3.6 Redis for caching and MongoDB for document data

questiontext.text:
To cut database load, a developer proposes reading account balances for payment authorisation from a Redis cache refreshed every 30 seconds.

What is the right response?

generalfeedback.text: A stale cached balance lets customers spend money they no longer have. Caches suit data where slight staleness is acceptable, never the authorisation decision for money.

answer.text: Approve it; 30 seconds is fresh enough
Approve it if Redis persistence (AOF) is on
Reject it: authorisation must use the source-of-truth balance inside the database transaction; caching is fine for display-only summaries

questiontext.text:
An account-summary cache uses cache-aside. After a deposit, customers sometimes see the old balance on the dashboard for up to an hour.

What is the most likely cause, and the fix?

generalfeedback.text: Without (correctly timed) invalidation the entry lives until its TTL. Deleting after commit means the next read reloads fresh data.

answer.text: The dashboard should poll more often
TTLs don't work for JSON values
The cache entry isn't invalidated (or is invalidated before the DB commit); delete the key after the posting commits, and keep a short TTL as a safety net

questiontext.text:
The FX-rate keys for 3,000 currency pairs are all cached with exactly 300 seconds TTL at the same moment. Every five minutes the database CPU spikes to 100%.

What is happening and how do you mitigate it?

generalfeedback.text: Keys set together expire together, sending all misses to the database at once. Jitter spreads expiry; a short recompute lock stops many requests rebuilding the same key.

answer.text: A cache stampede from synchronised expiry; add random jitter to TTLs and/or let only one request recompute a key

questiontext.text:
You must allow at most 5 failed PIN attempts per account per 15 minutes, across all instances of the service.

Which Redis approach is simplest and correct?

generalfeedback.text: INCR is atomic on the server, so concurrent failures from different instances count correctly; the expiry defines the window. GET-then-SET is a race; a local map isn't shared.

answer.text: GET the counter, add 1 in Java, SET it back
INCR pin:fail:<account> and set EXPIRE 900 on the first failure; block when the value exceeds 5
Store attempts in a local HashMap

questiontext.text:
A MongoDB account document embeds every transaction in an array. After two years, writes to busy accounts fail.

What modelling rule was broken?

generalfeedback.text: Embed bounded data that's read with the parent. Transactions grow without limit and are queried independently, so reference them instead.

answer.text: The account should be embedded in each transaction
Arrays are not allowed in MongoDB
The collection needs a TTL index
Unbounded, ever-growing data shouldn't be embedded; transactions belong in their own collection referencing the account (documents have a 16 MB limit and large documents are slow to update)

questiontext.text:
The KYC team's query find({status: 'PENDING_REVIEW', tier: 2}) takes seconds. explain('executionStats') shows COLLSCAN over 4 million documents.

What should you do?

generalfeedback.text: As in SQL, a query with no supporting index scans everything. A compound index on the filtered fields turns it into an index scan.

answer.text: Create a compound index such as { status: 1, tier: 1 } and confirm the plan shows IXSCAN

questiontext.text:
A mobile app retries POST /payments after a timeout, using the same Idempotency-Key header. You want the retry to return the original result instead of paying twice.

Which Redis command is the core of a simple idempotency check?

generalfeedback.text: SET ... NX succeeds only for the first request; a retry finds the key and returns the stored outcome. A unique reference in the database remains the final guarantee.

answer.text: SET idem:<key> IN_PROGRESS NX EX 86400 (set only if absent, with expiry)

questiontext.text:
A new onboarding service is being designed. You are asked which data belongs in which store.

Which pairings are sensible?

generalfeedback.text: Money needs relational ACID guarantees; expiring secrets fit Redis TTLs; flexible nested case files fit a document model. A ledger in Redis lists would lose constraints and durability guarantees.

answer.text: OTP codes valid for 2 minutes → Redis with a TTL
Varying KYC case files with nested documents and history → MongoDB (or PostgreSQL JSONB)

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.1 Dependency injection, IoC and auto-configuration

questiontext.text:
A new @Service in package ng.itlearning.payments isn't found at startup ('required a bean of type ... that could not be found'). The main class annotated @SpringBootApplication is in ng.itlearning.bank.app.

What is the most likely cause?

generalfeedback.text: Put the main class in the root package (e.g. ng.itlearning) so every feature package is beneath it, or configure scanning explicitly.

answer.text: The service needs @Autowired on the class
Component scanning starts from the main class's package and its sub-packages, so ng.itlearning.payments is never scanned

questiontext.text:
In code review you see @Autowired private AccountRepository repo; on a service. The reviewer asks for a change.

What is the preferred style and why?

generalfeedback.text: Constructor injection is the Spring team's recommendation. Field injection hides dependencies and forces reflection or a Spring context in tests.

answer.text: Setter injection, because it is more flexible
Constructor injection with a final field: dependencies are explicit, the object is complete after construction, and unit tests can use plain new
Keep field injection but make it public

questiontext.text:
A singleton @Service keeps private BigDecimal dailyTotal and adds each transfer's amount to it. Under load the totals are wrong.

What's the root cause?

generalfeedback.text: One instance serves every thread. Keep beans stateless; put shared state in the database, Redis or a thread-safe structure.

answer.text: Singleton beans are shared by all request threads, so mutable instance state is a race condition
Spring creates a new service per request

questiontext.text:
Two beans implement NotificationSender (SMS and email). Startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException at AlertService's constructor.

Which fixes are valid?

generalfeedback.text: Spring needs a way to choose: a default (@Primary), an explicit choice (@Qualifier), or a collection of all candidates.

answer.text: Mark one implementation @Primary, or use @Qualifier at the injection point, or inject List<NotificationSender> if all are needed

questiontext.text:
A team adds spring-boot-starter-data-redis for a cache in one feature. The next deploy fails health checks because the app tries to connect to Redis on localhost:6379.

Why did this happen?

generalfeedback.text: @ConditionalOnClass conditions switch on when a library appears. Configure the connection properties for each environment (or exclude the auto-configuration if unused).

answer.text: Auto-configuration is driven by the classpath: the starter's presence activated Redis auto-configuration with default connection properties

questiontext.text:
You define your own DataSource @Bean with a custom HikariCP configuration. A colleague worries Spring Boot will create a second DataSource too.

What actually happens?

generalfeedback.text: Auto-configuration is designed to step aside when you provide a bean of the same type. Prefer properties first, though: replacing the bean also replaces the defaults you got for free.

answer.text: The auto-configured DataSource is guarded by @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so it backs off and yours is used
Two DataSources are created and startup fails

questiontext.text:
You need to know why DataSourceAutoConfiguration did not apply in a test environment.

What is the quickest way to find out?

generalfeedback.text: The report lists every auto-configuration and the exact condition that matched or failed, for example 'did not find required class' or 'found bean of type DataSource'.

answer.text: Read every Spring Boot source file
Start the app with --debug (or check the actuator conditions endpoint) and read the conditions evaluation report's negative matches

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.2 HTTP and REST basics

questiontext.text:
A mobile app moves money with GET /transfer?from=0123456789&to=9876543210&amount=25000. Some customers are debited twice after their browser preloads links.

What is the root problem?

generalfeedback.text: Clients, proxies and browsers assume GET changes nothing and repeat it. Actions that move money use POST; payment details also don't belong in URLs, which end up in logs.

answer.text: The amount should be in kobo
GET must be safe: it may be repeated or prefetched freely, so creating a transfer must use POST /transfers with a JSON body
The query string is too long
The server should cache the response

questiontext.text:
A transfer API answers every request with 200 OK, including {"status":"FAILED","reason":"INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS"}. The operations dashboard shows a 0% error rate during an incident.

What should the API do instead?

generalfeedback.text: Monitoring, client libraries and other engineers rely on the status code. Business-rule rejections are client errors (4xx); 500 is for server failures.

answer.text: Use status codes that mean what happened, for example 201 for a created transfer and 422 for insufficient funds, with an error body

questiontext.text:
A request without a token gets one status code; a logged-in customer asking for someone else's account gets another.

Which pair is correct?

generalfeedback.text: 401 means "we don't know who you are"; 403 means "we know who you are, and you can't do this". Some banks return 404 for others' accounts so they don't reveal that the account exists.

questiontext.text:
A JavaScript client reads "amount": 0.1 and "fee": 0.2 from your JSON and shows a total of 0.30000000000000004.

How should the API represent money?

generalfeedback.text: Many clients parse JSON numbers as binary floating point. Strings or integer minor units keep amounts exact; Jackson reads either into a BigDecimal or long.

answer.text: As JSON numbers with more decimal places
As strings such as "25000.00", or as integer minor units such as 2500000 kobo

questiontext.text:
A service calls a KYC provider with Java's HttpClient. During the provider's outage, all of the service's threads hang and it stops answering.

What was missing?

generalfeedback.text: Without timeouts a call can wait forever. Fail fast, check the status code, and (topic 5.4) add retries and circuit breakers on top.

answer.text: Timeouts: a connect timeout on the client and a request timeout, so a slow partner fails fast

questiontext.text:
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/accounts/0123456789/balance returns 405. The same URL works with GET.

What does 405 mean here?

generalfeedback.text: 405 Method Not Allowed: the resource is there, but only the mapped methods (here GET) are accepted. A path with no mapping at all gives 404.

answer.text: The path exists but doesn't support the POST method

questiontext.text:
A client successfully creates a transfer with POST /transfers.

Which response is most RESTful?

generalfeedback.text: 201 tells the client a new resource exists, and Location says where to read it later with GET.

answer.text: 201 Created with a Location: /transfers/TRF-2026-00042 header and the new transfer as JSON
302 Found redirecting to the home page

questiontext.text:
A mobile app sends POST /transfers, then its connection drops before the response arrives. It can't tell whether the transfer was made.

Why is blindly retrying risky, and what's the standard fix?

generalfeedback.text: GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent by definition; POST is not. An idempotency key lets the server return the original result for a repeated request instead of paying twice.

answer.text: It isn't risky; POST is idempotent
POST isn't idempotent, so a retry may create a second transfer; APIs use an idempotency key so the server recognises the repeat (topic 5.3)
Switch to GET so retries are safe

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.3 Spring MVC controllers, validation and global error handling

questiontext.text:
A TransferRequest record has @NotNull @DecimalMin("1.00") BigDecimal amount, yet requests with negative amounts reach the service.

What is the most likely omission?

generalfeedback.text: Constraint annotations are only checked when validation is triggered. @Valid on the @RequestBody parameter tells Spring MVC to validate it before calling the method.

answer.text: Validation only works on GET requests
The record must be a class
The controller parameter lacks @Valid (e.g. @Valid @RequestBody TransferRequest request)

questiontext.text:
A controller returns the JPA Account entity directly. A tester sends a PUT with "balance": 9999999 and "status": "ACTIVE" for a frozen account, and both change.

What design fix prevents this?

generalfeedback.text: Binding requests straight onto entities enables mass assignment. DTOs define the contract explicitly; entities stay internal.

answer.text: Use separate request/response DTOs (records) that contain only the fields clients may send or see, and map explicitly
Mark the fields @JsonIgnore one by one as problems are found

questiontext.text:
A transfer request is well-formed, but the source account doesn't have enough money.

Which status code best represents this business-rule failure?

generalfeedback.text: The syntax is valid; the request cannot be processed because of the current state. 422 (or 409 for state conflicts) communicates that. 400 is for malformed or invalid input; 500 means a server bug.

questiontext.text:
Mobile developers complain that errors come back in five different JSON shapes depending on the endpoint, and some include Java stack traces.

What is the best fix?

generalfeedback.text: A single advice class gives one consistent, standards-based format, keeps controllers clean, and is the one place to make sure nothing internal leaks.

answer.text: Wrap every controller method in try/catch
Let Tomcat's default error page handle it
One @RestControllerAdvice that maps exceptions to RFC 9457 ProblemDetail responses (spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true for Spring's own exceptions), never exposing stack traces

questiontext.text:
You want a fast test that a controller returns 400 with field errors for an invalid body, without starting the database or real services.

Which test setup fits?

generalfeedback.text: @WebMvcTest loads only the web slice (controllers, advice, validation, JSON conversion). @MockitoBean replaces the service. Calling the method directly would bypass validation and JSON handling.

answer.text: A plain JUnit test calling the controller method directly
@WebMvcTest(TransferController.class) with the service replaced by @MockitoBean, using MockMvc

questiontext.text:
After upgrading to Spring Boot 4, a test using @MockBean TransferService service; no longer compiles.

What is the replacement?

generalfeedback.text: Spring Boot 4 removed @MockBean and @SpyBean in favour of Spring Framework's @MockitoBean and @MockitoSpyBean.

questiontext.text:
A field BigDecimal amount should accept ₦10.50 but reject ₦10.555, so rounding never happens silently later.

Which constraint enforces that at the API boundary?

generalfeedback.text: @Digits limits integer and fraction digits for numeric types. @Size applies to strings and collections; @Pattern applies to strings.

questiontext.text:
A team uses MapStruct. A new field riskScore is added to the response DTO, but responses always show it as null and nothing failed.

What configuration would have caught this?

generalfeedback.text: MapStruct reports unmapped targets as warnings by default; making them errors catches missing mappings at compile time.

answer.text: unmappedTargetPolicy = ReportingPolicy.ERROR, so unmapped target properties fail the build
Making the DTO a class instead of a record

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.4 Spring Data JPA and Hibernate

questiontext.text:
An endpoint lists 500 active accounts with each customer's name. SQL logs show one select from account, then 500 nearly identical select ... from customer where id=? statements.

What is this, and which fix loads the data in one query?

generalfeedback.text: Each lazy access fires its own query. Fetching the association in the original query (or projecting the needed columns) turns 501 round trips into one.

answer.text: Connection pool exhaustion; raise the pool size
The N+1 select problem; use a fetch join (join fetch a.customer), an @EntityGraph, or a DTO projection

questiontext.text:
A product enum is reordered (CURRENT moved before SAVINGS). Afterwards, every savings account displays as current.

What mapping caused this, and what should be used?

generalfeedback.text: ORDINAL stores 0, 1, 2, which changes meaning when the enum changes. STRING stores the constant's name and is stable.

answer.text: Enums can't be persisted; use strings

questiontext.text:
TransferService.transferAll() loops and calls this.transfer(...), which is annotated @Transactional. Logs show that no transaction is ever started: a failure between the debit and the credit leaves the debit saved.

Why didn't @Transactional apply?

generalfeedback.text: Transactional behaviour is added by a proxy around the bean. Internal this.method() calls don't go through it. Move the method to another bean or put the transaction on the outer method.

answer.text: Self-invocation bypasses the Spring proxy, so the annotation on transfer() is never applied when called from inside the same bean

questiontext.text:
A service method annotated @Transactional throws a checked StatementGenerationException after inserting rows. The rows remain in the database.

Why?

generalfeedback.text: Spring's default mirrors EJB conventions: checked exceptions commit. Prefer unchecked domain exceptions, or configure rollbackFor explicitly.

answer.text: By default Spring rolls back only on unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and Error); use an unchecked exception or rollbackFor
The exception was thrown too late

questiontext.text:
Two back-office agents edit the same customer profile. The second save silently overwrites the first agent's changes.

Which JPA feature detects this conflict?

generalfeedback.text: @Version adds 'AND version = ?' to the UPDATE. If someone else committed first, no row matches and Hibernate throws, instead of losing an update.

answer.text: A @Version field (optimistic locking); the stale update fails with an optimistic-locking exception you can map to 409

questiontext.text:
A developer sets spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update in production 'so new columns appear automatically'.

What should the team do instead?

generalfeedback.text: update makes unreviewed, unversioned, sometimes destructive schema changes and can't handle renames or data migrations. Migrations are reviewed and repeatable; validate catches drift.

answer.text: Manage the schema with Flyway (or Liquibase) migrations and set ddl-auto=validate so startup fails on mismatches
Use none and edit the database by hand
Keep update but back up daily

questiontext.text:
A statement endpoint returns account.getTransactions() (a @OneToMany collection) as JSON. For a 6-year-old business account, it takes 40 seconds and uses gigabytes of memory.

What is the better design?

generalfeedback.text: Unbounded collections should be queried, not navigated. A paged projection loads only the requested page of columns.

answer.text: Query transactions with a paged, filtered repository method (ideally a DTO projection) instead of loading the whole collection

questiontext.text:
You're reviewing a new JPA entity class.

Which of these are problems?

generalfeedback.text: Final classes prevent Hibernate's proxies; toString on lazy associations triggers loading (or LazyInitializationException); @ManyToOne defaults to EAGER. A protected no-arg constructor is correct.

answer.text: toString() prints the lazy accounts collection
It has a protected no-arg constructor

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.5 Configuration, profiles and secrets handling

questiontext.text:
A developer commits spring.datasource.password=Prod#2026! to application-prod.yaml in a private GitHub repo, then deletes the line in the next commit.

What is the correct response?

generalfeedback.text: Git history keeps the secret and it may already be cloned or scanned. Rotation is the only real fix; history rewriting and process changes follow.

answer.text: Treat it as a leak: rotate the database password immediately, then remove it from history and move secrets to the environment or a secrets manager
Base64-encode the password in the file

questiontext.text:
application.yaml sets bank.transfer.daily-limit: 5000000. In production the platform sets environment variable BANK_TRANSFER_DAILYLIMIT=2000000, and the app is started with --bank.transfer.daily-limit=1000000.

Which value does the application use?

generalfeedback.text: Command-line arguments override environment variables, which override application.yaml packaged in the jar.

answer.text: Startup fails due to the conflict

questiontext.text:
You need to set the property bank.partners.nibss.base-url from a Kubernetes environment variable.

Which variable name does Spring Boot's relaxed binding map to it?

generalfeedback.text: Uppercase, dots to underscores, dashes removed. Dashes aren't valid in most shells' variable names.

questiontext.text:
Transfer limits are read with @Value in six classes. A typo in a UAT config file (daily-limt) isn't noticed until transfers start failing in the afternoon.

Which approach would have caught it at startup?

generalfeedback.text: Type-safe, validated configuration binds the group in one place; a missing required value stops the app before it takes traffic.

answer.text: A @ConfigurationProperties record for bank.transfer with @Validated and @NotNull constraints, so missing or invalid values fail startup

questiontext.text:
The team has application-dev.yaml, application-uat.yaml, application-preprod.yaml and application-prod.yaml, each with URLs and credentials, all inside the jar.

What's the main improvement?

generalfeedback.text: The same artefact should run anywhere, with environment-specific values supplied by the environment. Production credentials should never be inside the build.

answer.text: Merge all files into one with if-statements
Keep environment-specific values (URLs, credentials, sizes) out of the jar and inject them via environment variables or a secrets manager; use profiles sparingly for behaviour differences

questiontext.text:
A property is declared as password: ${DB_PASSWORD:admin123} 'so the app always starts'.

Why is this a problem?

generalfeedback.text: A missing secret is a misconfiguration and should stop startup. A default hides the problem and may even work against a misconfigured database.

answer.text: If the secret isn't provided, the app silently uses a guessable password instead of failing fast; secrets should have no defaults outside local-only config

questiontext.text:
A new joiner needs to know which environment variables the service requires to run locally, but no secrets may be committed.

What is the standard approach?

generalfeedback.text: The example file documents required settings without real values; each developer creates their own git-ignored .env.

answer.text: Put the values in the README
Commit a .env.example with placeholder values and keep the real .env git-ignored
Hard-code local values in the main class

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.6 Spring Boot Actuator

questiontext.text:
During a 10-minute PostgreSQL outage, Kubernetes restarted every instance of the payments API repeatedly, and recovery took longer than the outage. The db health indicator was in the liveness group.

What should the probe configuration be?

generalfeedback.text: Restarting can't fix a database outage. Readiness takes instances out of rotation; liveness should reflect only the process's own health.

answer.text: Make liveness call the database twice
Keep external dependencies like the database out of liveness; include them in readiness so instances stop receiving traffic but aren't restarted
Put the database in both groups

questiontext.text:
A security scan finds https://api.bank.example/actuator/heapdump publicly downloadable.

Why is this critical, and what's the fix?

generalfeedback.text: Exposed actuator endpoints are a known attack path. Minimise exposure (health, info, prometheus), restrict network access and require authentication for the rest.

answer.text: It's harmless; heap dumps only contain class names
A heap dump contains everything in memory (tokens, passwords, customer data); expose only needed endpoints, move management to an internal port, secure it, and disable heapdump in production

questiontext.text:
A developer adds a metric bank.transfers tagged with account (the account number) and reference. Prometheus memory usage explodes within a day.

What went wrong?

generalfeedback.text: Each unique tag combination is a separate series. Per-account or per-reference data belongs in logs, traces or the database, not metric tags.

answer.text: High-cardinality tags: every unique account/reference creates a new time series; tag only with small fixed sets such as outcome and channel
The metric name contains a dot

questiontext.text:
You need to measure how long calls to the card switch take, including p95 and p99 across all instances.

Which Micrometer meter fits?

generalfeedback.text: A Timer records counts and durations; publishing a histogram lets Prometheus aggregate percentiles across instances correctly.

answer.text: Timer with a percentile histogram published

questiontext.text:
During an incident you need DEBUG logs for ng.itlearning.bank.transfer for 10 minutes without redeploying.

Which Actuator endpoint helps?

generalfeedback.text: The loggers endpoint reads and changes log levels at runtime. Because it changes behaviour, it must be secured.

questiontext.text:
The operations team wants to see how many payment jobs are waiting in an in-memory queue at any moment.

Which meter type represents that?

generalfeedback.text: A gauge reports a current value that can go up and down, such as queue size. Counters only increase.

questiontext.text:
Support often asks 'which version and commit is running in UAT?' and nobody knows without checking the CI logs.

What's the simplest fix?

generalfeedback.text: Spring Boot reads META-INF/build-info.properties and git.properties and shows them on /actuator/info, giving an instant answer.

answer.text: Generate build-info (and git properties) with the Maven plugins and expose the info endpoint internally
Add the version to every log line manually
Name the jar after the commit
Ask the release manager each time

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.7 What changed from Spring Boot 3 to 4, and how to upgrade

questiontext.text:
After upgrading a service from Boot 3.5 to 4.1, it starts cleanly, but new tables from migration V12 never appear. The POM still has org.flywaydb:flyway-core and no Flyway starter.

What is the cause and fix?

generalfeedback.text: In Boot 4, technologies that used to activate from the bare library need their starter. Without it the auto-configuration isn't on the classpath and migrations silently don't run.

answer.text: Boot 4's modular auto-configuration only applies Flyway with spring-boot-starter-flyway; add it (plus flyway-database-postgresql)
Migrations must be renamed for Boot 4
Flyway is not supported in Boot 4

questiontext.text:
Tests using @MockBean PaymentGateway gateway; stop compiling after the upgrade.

What replaces it?

generalfeedback.text: Boot 4 removed @MockBean/@SpyBean. Spring Framework's @MockitoBean/@MockitoSpyBean replace them, with slightly different rules (for example, not on @Configuration classes).

answer.text: Nothing; mocking beans isn't possible in Boot 4
@MockitoBean (and @MockitoSpyBean for spies) from Spring Framework's test support

questiontext.text:
A @SpringBootTest that autowires MockMvc fails after the upgrade with 'No qualifying bean of type MockMvc'.

What change is needed?

generalfeedback.text: In Boot 4, @SpringBootTest no longer configures MockMvc on its own; @AutoConfigureMockMvc opts in explicitly.

answer.text: Add @AutoConfigureMockMvc to the test class (and the webmvc test starter)
Create MockMvc manually in every test

questiontext.text:
A custom Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer bean no longer affects JSON output after the upgrade.

Why, and what's the Boot 4 equivalent?

generalfeedback.text: Jackson 3 changed packages and Boot renamed the customiser. Defining an ObjectMapper bean is no longer enough to replace the auto-configured JsonMapper.

answer.text: Use an ObjectMapper bean; it always wins
Boot 4 uses Jackson 3 and auto-configures a JsonMapper; use a JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer (tools.jackson packages) instead

questiontext.text:
You inherit a service on Spring Boot 3.1 and must move it to 4.1.

What should the first step be?

generalfeedback.text: APIs deprecated in 3.x were removed in 4.0. Upgrading within 3.x first surfaces them as warnings, while everything still compiles.

answer.text: Change the parent version straight to 4.1.x
Upgrade to the latest 3.5.x, fix all deprecation warnings and get a green build
Switch to the classic starters permanently

questiontext.text:
After the upgrade, startup logs show several warnings about renamed configuration keys, which your team wants to find quickly and fix.

Which tool helps, and how should it be used?

generalfeedback.text: The migrator reports changed/removed properties and maps them temporarily at runtime. It's a migration aid, not something to ship long term.

answer.text: Keep the properties migrator permanently in production
Add spring-boot-properties-migrator temporarily, fix the reported properties in config files, then remove it

questiontext.text:
The API team is worried that dates, nulls or BigDecimal formatting in responses might change silently with the Jackson 3 switch.

What is the best safety net to add before upgrading?

generalfeedback.text: Contract tests make any change in serialisation fail the build, so you can decide deliberately (or set use-jackson2-defaults) rather than discovering it in client apps.

answer.text: Manual testing in Postman after deploy
JSON contract (snapshot) tests that serialise known objects and compare them with stored expected JSON

questiontext.text:
A team lists changes they expect when moving from Boot 3.5 to Boot 4.x.

Which of these are real Boot 4 changes?

generalfeedback.text: Boot 4 still requires Java 17 as a minimum (21 or 25 recommended). The other three are documented changes.

answer.text: Jakarta EE 11 baseline with Spring Framework 7
spring-boot-starter-web renamed to spring-boot-starter-webmvc (old name deprecated)

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.8 Spring under the hood

questiontext.text:
A @Transactional method saves a statement header and then calls Files.readAllLines(file), which throws IOException. The header row stays in the database.

Why, and what is the fix?

generalfeedback.text: Checked exceptions commit by default; declare rollback rules explicitly when they must undo work.

answer.text: By default Spring rolls back only on unchecked exceptions; add rollbackFor = Exception.class (or IOException.class)
readOnly must be set to true

questiontext.text:
An audit insert is marked @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW) and called from transfer() in the same class. When the transfer fails, the audit row disappears too.

Why?

generalfeedback.text: Self-invocation never reaches the proxy that would start the new transaction.

answer.text: The call goes through this, bypassing the proxy, so the audit runs in the transfer's transaction; move it to a separate bean

questiontext.text:
An outer @Transactional method calls feeService.apply() (also @Transactional, default propagation), catches its RuntimeException and continues. On commit Spring throws UnexpectedRollbackException.

What happened?

generalfeedback.text: With REQUIRED both methods share one transaction; an inner failure marks it rollback-only.

answer.text: The inner method joined the same transaction and marked it rollback-only when it threw; catching the exception didn't undo that
Propagation REQUIRED always throws on commit

questiontext.text:
A singleton service has a prototype-scoped ReportBuilder injected through its constructor, expecting a fresh builder per request. Reports start mixing data.

What is wrong?

generalfeedback.text: Injection happens once; ask the container for a new prototype instance when you need one.

answer.text: Constructor injection is not allowed for prototypes
The prototype was injected once when the singleton was created; use ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder>.getObject() each time

questiontext.text:
A nightly @Scheduled interest job is deployed on two pods behind a load balancer. Customers receive interest twice.

What is the best fix?

generalfeedback.text: Every instance runs every @Scheduled method; distributed locking plus idempotency prevents double posting.

answer.text: Ensure only one instance runs it (ShedLock or a database advisory lock, or a platform scheduler) and make the job idempotent

questiontext.text:
A transfer service sends a confirmation SMS from an @EventListener. Some customers get SMSs for transfers that later rolled back.

What should change?

generalfeedback.text: Plain @EventListener runs synchronously inside the publisher's transaction.

answer.text: Use @TransactionalEventListener (AFTER_COMMIT) so the listener runs only after a successful commit

questiontext.text:
Which statements about Spring proxies are true? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Proxies wrap Spring-managed beans after initialisation and only intercept external calls to proxyable methods.

answer.text: Self-invocation always goes through the proxy
Proxies are created before the constructor runs
Annotations like @Transactional and @Cacheable don't apply to private methods
Objects created with new don't get Spring's proxy-based behaviour

questiontext.text:
A service is missing a DataSource at start-up after an upgrade, and the team can't tell why auto-configuration skipped it.

What is the quickest way to find out?

generalfeedback.text: The report lists which auto-configurations matched or didn't, and the condition responsible.

answer.text: Start with --debug (or the Actuator conditions endpoint) and read the conditions evaluation report

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 1/4.9 Spring Boot with Kotlin

questiontext.text:
A Kotlin Spring service's @Configuration class fails at startup with an error about a final class that can't be subclassed for proxying.

What is missing from the build?

generalfeedback.text: Kotlin classes are final by default. Spring proxies @Configuration, @Transactional and similar classes by subclassing them; the all-open plugin opens them automatically.

answer.text: The Kotlin 'spring' (all-open) compiler plugin, which opens Spring-annotated classes for proxying

questiontext.text:
A Kotlin DTO declares data class TransferRequest(@NotBlank val narration: String, ...). Blank narrations pass validation in an older Kotlin project.

What is the reliable fix?

generalfeedback.text: Constructor properties generate a parameter, field and getter. Without an explicit target the annotation may land on the constructor parameter only; @field: puts it where Hibernate Validator looks.

answer.text: Use the field use-site target: @field:NotBlank, so the constraint is placed on the field Bean Validation inspects

questiontext.text:
A developer maps Account as a Kotlin data class with a lazy @ManyToOne customer. Logging an account outside a transaction throws LazyInitializationException.

Why, and what's the recommended mapping?

generalfeedback.text: Data classes generate members over all constructor properties. For entities, write equals/hashCode/toString explicitly and keep associations out of them.

answer.text: Lazy loading isn't supported in Kotlin
The generated toString/equals/hashCode touch every property, including the lazy association; use a regular class with a hand-written toString/equals based on a business key

questiontext.text:
A Kotlin JPA entity fails with 'No default constructor for entity'.

Which build configuration solves it without writing constructors by hand?

generalfeedback.text: JPA providers need a no-arg constructor. The jpa plugin generates a synthetic one for @Entity, @Embeddable and @MappedSuperclass classes.

questiontext.text:
In Kotlin, a Spring Data repository method needs to return 'no account found' for an unknown number.

What is the idiomatic return type?

generalfeedback.text: Spring Data supports nullable return types in Kotlin. The Elvis operator then makes the missing case explicit and concise.

questiontext.text:
POST requests to a Kotlin controller fail with a JSON deserialisation error about missing a no-args constructor for the request data class.

What is most likely missing?

generalfeedback.text: The Kotlin Jackson module lets Jackson call primary constructors with named, non-null and default parameters. start.spring.io includes it for Kotlin projects.

answer.text: jackson-module-kotlin on the classpath (Spring Boot registers it automatically when present)
